subject: Using model to make predictions against new data

messages.author: 6b47fc5f010c683c
messages.subject: Using model to make predictions against new data
parts:
I'm sure this is a very basic question, but I'm new to both Deducer and R so it has me stuck. I've developed a prediction model using logistic regression that I'm happy with (.86 AUC) and now I want to apply it to some test data where the outcome is hidden (same data structure, no scrubbing necessary, etc. The only thing different between the two sets is that test is missing the outcome variable). This is where I'm having trouble...I don't see any way to do this through the Deducer GUI. Am I missing something or must any kind of forecasting/prediction be done directly in the console? I can export predictions easily enough if I go through Analysis->Logistic Model->Export->Prediction but this route requires me to select an outcome variable. If I don't have an outcome then I can't go this route through the interface.

If the console is the only way apply the model so that it actually produces predictions against a test dataset, can anyone give me some tips/steps/example code? Basically I want exactly the same prediction output that you can export when you run the logistic regression procedure. But I want it against data that doesn't already have the dv defined.

Thank you!

messages.author: 10e4228dbae00b18
messages.subject: Re: Using model to make predictions against new data
parts:
Here's more specific information in hopes that it'll help in providing an answer:

I have two data sets: 1) "train", and 2) "test"

I am trying to predict the likelihood of survival for individual passengers on the Titanic based on a few variables (age, sex, and passenger class)

When I create the model I use the following:

model.glm <- glm(forumula=survived==1 ~ pclass + age + sex,family=binomial(),data=train,na.action=na.omit)

I can then output the predictions by using the following:

tmp <- predict(model.glm,type="response")
train[names(tmp),"predicted")<-tmp

So far so good. Now, however, I want to apply the model to my "test" data set. Here is where I run into trouble.

tmpTest <- predict(model.glm, type="response")
test[names(tmpTest),"predicted")<-tmpTest

When I write that code, it looks like the predictions are fine BUT I actually get the same predictions in the same order as I did with the "train" data set even though the "test" data set is completely different. So while I'm trying to apply the model to the "test" data set and ouput predictions to that set, instead it looks like I'm just applying the model to the "train" data set again and outputing the predictions for "train" to "test"

What am I doing wrong?

messages.author: 267c7c6c510dc8a2
messages.subject: Re: Using model to make predictions against new data
parts:
Currently Deducer does not suport out-of-dataset predictions, though it is on my TODO list. you can do these in R with:

test$prediction <- predict(model.glm,newdata=test)


best,
ian

messages.subject: Re: Using model to make predictions against new data
parts:
Thanks, Ian. I find that if I use the following, I get the results in the format I'm expecting:

model.glm <- glm(formula=survived>0.0 ~ pclass + age + sex,family=binomial(),data=train,na.action=na.omit)
tmp <- predict(model.glm,test,type="response")
test[names(tmp),"predicted"]<-tmp

However, if I use the following I get prediction values that don't makes sense (negative numbers):

model.glm <- glm(formula=survived>0.0 ~ pclass + age + sex,family=binomial(),data=train,na.action=na.omit)
test$prediction <- predict(model.glm,newdata=test)

It seems like both of these should be doing almost the same thing. Do you know why the numbers would be different?
